text:
The Maple Leafs just finished the worst homestand in their 109-year history, capped by a 1-0 loss to Edmonton, and now the questions are about everything. Should Jim Hiller be fired? Is Auston Matthews' future in Toronto in doubt, as one insider suggested? William Nylander is answering trade questions in the middle of a slump. Matthews has publicly backed his coach.

Toronto is 8-12-2 with 18 points and winless in six (0-6-0), outscored 23-9. Unlike some slumping teams, this one is earned: 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during the streak, 46% at five on five for the season. Our playoff odds are at 4%.

The crease hasn't bailed them out. Sergei Bobrovsky is 0-5-0 over his last five starts with .857 and 4.6 goals worse than expected. The Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh pair plays the most and has been outscored 13-8.

What still works runs through Matthews. His line with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan has outscored teams 9-3, and Roslovic has points in eight of his last nine games. Gavin McKenna, the rookie everyone wanted to see, has been honest about playing fewer minutes during the skid and says he feels himself growing on both sides of the puck. What we'd watch: McKenna's ice time, and whether the front office makes a change behind the bench before the season gets away completely.
